claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a close derivative has high saturation magnetization and coercivity at or below approximately 100 Oe.
Controlled aging at approximately 500–700 °C for several hours can nucleate a secondary ordered precipitate phase in an fcc FeCoNi-based matrix.
Aging can produce coherent nanoscale precipitates in a high-entropy alloy.
Adding a few atomic percent Al can facilitate ordering in the proposed FeCoNi-based alloy.
The precipitates can have a B2-type or similar ordered structure while the matrix remains predominantly fcc.
The ordered nanoprecipitates generate local strain fields.
The ordered nanoprecipitates create localized regions of enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
The precipitate-associated strain and anisotropy pin magnetic domain walls.
Domain-wall pinning raises the energy barrier for magnetization reversal.
The increased reversal barrier raises the coercive field.
The treated alloy will have a coercive field at least 50% greater than the untreated control, potentially exceeding 100 Oe.
The treated alloy will retain high saturation magnetization without a significant reduction relative to untreated single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
Coarse phase separation could detrimentally affect magnetic or structural properties.
The proposed treatment is constrained to preserve a predominantly fcc matrix and produce only uniformly distributed coherent nanoscale precipitates.
Room-temperature VSM hysteresis measurements will be used to compare coercivity and saturation magnetization between aged and untreated samples.
TEM and XRD will be used to determine whether the expected precipitates formed.
A coercivity increase of less than 50% relative to the untreated control is designated as a falsifying outcome.
Failure to detect coherent nanoprecipitates is designated as falsification of the hypothesis.
